root_cause.text: smc_clc_wait_msg() assumed smc->conn.lgr was already initialized when handling a first-contact CLC decline, causing premature access to uncreated link-group state during early SMC handshake.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the decline path from updating smc->conn.lgr->sync_err solely on SMC_FIRST_CONTACT_MASK to doing so only when “smc->conn.lgr” is non-NULL, and the CVE/commit message explicitly says a decline can arrive “before the connection has been associated with a link group” while “that state only exists after link group setup has completed.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a link-group null check before flagging and terminating it on first-contact decline handling.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a direct cast-and-access of `((struct smc_clc_msg_decline *)buf)->hdr.typev2` with the already assigned local variable `dclc->hdr.typev2`, and adds an additional condition `smc->conn.lgr` to the `if` statement before setting `smc->conn.lgr->sync_err` and calling `smc_lgr_terminate_sched()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the decline-message handling now only marks the link group as having a sync error and schedules its termination when the first-contact flag is set and a valid link-group pointer exists, preventing dereferencing a null `smc->conn.lgr` while preserving the existing behavior for valid link groups.

    smc_lgr_terminate() and smc_lgr_terminate_sched() both result in soft

The stated root cause is that smc_clc_wait_msg() assumed `smc->conn.lgr` was already initialized during a first-contact CLC decline, leading to premature access to uncreated link-group state.
